acceptance.given: An applicable Consumer has enabled the Candidate Route and has no approved non-applicability exception.

oracle.expected: A real Consumer invocation calls the Prior Route for disable and records successful disable execution.
forbidden: Disable is executed only through a simulated, configuration-only, or non-real call surface.
oracle.observable: The Consumer's real disable invocation record, including invoked Prior Route identity and result.

acceptance.then: Disable is executed by the applicable Consumer through a real call surface.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the disable-transition selector with a configuration-only or simulated disable path and observe failure.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Route each applicable Consumer's disable transition through its real call surface to the Prior Route and capture the invocation result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve Consumer replay receipt compatibility and existing disable-transition semantics.

slice_hint.state_transition: Candidate Route enabled for an applicable Consumer -> Consumer invokes the Prior Route through its real disable call surface -> disable observation is recorded.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Each applicable Consumer's disable transition has a real Prior Route invocation record; simulated or configuration-only disable is rejected.

acceptance.given: A Toolchain write operation is proposed against each protected Phase, runtime, Hosted workspace, account, and user-sandbox path category.

oracle.expected: Every attempted write is deterministically rejected, leaves the target unchanged, and reports a boundary violation; the same enforcement applies across all five protected categories.
forbidden: Any Phase, runtime, Hosted workspace, account, or user-sandbox file is modified under this scope.
oracle.observable: The boundary validator returns a rejection for each protected-path fixture and byte/state comparison confirms no protected file changed.

acceptance.then: The protected-path boundary check is evaluated before any filesystem mutation is permitted.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain boundary validator is executed against the protected-path fixtures.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Use the protected-path negative validator to demonstrate that a proposed write to a Phase, runtime, Hosted workspace, account, or user-sandbox path is accepted instead of rejected.
Use the protected-path negative validator to detect any protected target whose bytes or existence changed after the attempted write.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce a Toolchain-only, fail-closed write boundary: before filesystem mutation, classify repository-relative targets and reject all Phase, runtime, Hosted workspace, account, and user-sandbox paths while preserving protected-target bytes and state. The check must not authorize or modify Phase service or sandbox code.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Rollback removes only the boundary-enforcement change and preserves existing receipt, schema, and lifecycle semantics; no protected path or live database state is altered.

slice_hint.state_transition: proposed write -> protected-path classification -> deterministic rejection with no mutation
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: All five protected path categories produce rejection results and byte/state checks show no protected target changed; any accepted write or mutation is a failed terminal result.

acceptance.given: A requested target resolves outside its permitted repository scope or boundary.

oracle.expected: The operation rejects or blocks the escaping target before any target-dependent operation proceeds.
forbidden: Allowing the target to cross its permitted boundary.
oracle.observable: The target-validation decision and absence of an accepted or used escaping target.

acceptance.then: The escaping-target condition is rejected and no target-dependent operation proceeds.
acceptance.when: A target path escapes its permitted scope or boundary.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the target-validation selector with a traversal target and observe fail-closed rejection.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate repository-relative target containment and fail closed before an escaping target can be accepted or used.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve repository-relative target semantics; escaping targets remain invalid-input failures.

slice_hint.state_transition: Escaping target supplied -> containment validation runs -> target is rejected and target-dependent execution does not proceed.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The traversal target is rejected before use and no target-dependent operation occurs.

acceptance.given: A Replay Result succeeds for an input whose Validator Capability is independently evaluable.

oracle.expected: The replay result includes a Validator Capability verification outcome produced for that result, independently of other replay verifications.
forbidden: A successful Replay Result whose Validator Capability verification is inferred from another verification.
oracle.observable: The successful replay result's per-result Validator Capability verification outcome.

acceptance.then: The successful Replay Result carries its own Validator Capability verification outcome.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the S24 replay behavior test with a successful replay whose Validator Capability outcome is omitted or borrowed; the runtime assertion must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require each successful replay result to independently verify and expose its Validator Capability outcome.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Restore prior replay-result verification handling without changing the capability descriptor schema.

slice_hint.state_transition: successful replay without independent capability verification -> successful replay with a per-result independent capability outcome
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The S24 selector rejects a successful replay that lacks its own Validator Capability verification.
